behavior: Mostly nocturnal and often solitary outside nesting; hunts from perches with quiet, broad-winged flight, taking mainly mammals and birds. Territorial pairs advertise and defend their range with deep hoots.
field_marks: Large, thick-bodied owl with prominent ear tufts and an upright posture
Bright yellow eyes set in a gray-to-cinnamon facial disc
Short, dark, hooked bill partly concealed by facial feathers
Mottled gray-brown upperparts, a white throat patch, and densely barred underparts
Broad, rounded wings and a relatively short, barred tail
Heavily feathered legs ending in powerful dark talons
habitat: Highly adaptable; favors mosaics of woodland and open ground but also uses forests, wetlands, grasslands, deserts, agricultural areas, and wooded developed areas. Roosts and nests in trees, cavities, snags, ledges, and abandoned nests.
